TIT.1.1-3.text: Paul introduces himself as God’s servant and apostle

TIT.1.4-4.text: Paul greets Titus, his true child in the faith

TIT.1.5-5.text: Paul left Titus in Crete to appoint elders

TIT.1.6-7.text: Elders must be blameless in family and character

TIT.1.8-9.text: Elders must live well and hold to the true message

TIT.1.10-11.text: Rebellious people who mislead households must be silenced

TIT.1.12-13.text: Titus must firmly correct them so their faith is sound

TIT.1.14-14.text: Do not follow myths or commands of men

TIT.1.15-16.text: Some say they know God but their actions deny him

TIT.2.1-2.text: Titus teaches older men to live with self-control

TIT.2.3-5.text: Older women are to teach the younger women

TIT.2.6-8.text: Titus urges younger men and sets an example

TIT.2.9-10.text: Slaves are to be respectful and honest to their masters

TIT.2.11-13.text: God’s grace teaches us to live well as we wait for Christ

TIT.2.14-14.text: Christ gave himself to make a people for himself

TIT.3.1-2.text: Believers should obey rulers and be gentle to everyone

TIT.3.3-3.text: Before, we were foolish and slaves to our desires

TIT.3.4-5.text: God saved us because of his mercy, not our deeds

TIT.3.6-7.text: God poured out the Spirit so we have hope of eternal life

TIT.3.8-8.text: Believers should be devoted to doing good

TIT.3.9-11.text: Avoid foolish arguments and reject a divisive person

TIT.3.12-13.text: Paul asks Titus to come and to help Zenas and Apollos

TIT.3.14-14.text: Believers must work to meet urgent needs
